brief: Deutsche Bank argues the US is funding the AI race through capitalism itself. US companies are expected to spend around $800bn on AI capex this year against roughly $100bn in China, so the US is raising record private capital: over $400bn of AI venture funding, hyperscaler investment grade debt near ten times the 2020-24 average, and Google's first primary equity raise since its 2004 IPO. With a 6%+ fiscal deficit and a near 4% of GDP current account deficit, that capex needs foreign funding, and Q2 2026 brought over USD400bn of foreign equity inflows. Blockchain is the lever. Stablecoins put the dollar on chain, and asset tokenization, now live at the DTC and the exchanges under SEC cover, lowers the hurdles for inbound capital by making US assets more collateral efficient and accessible 24/7. The bank's conclusion is two-sided. Easier entry also means easier exit, so the dollar becomes riskier, more equity sensitive and leveraged to the AI race, and exposed if AI proves uneconomical. Separately, China's low-cost open-weight models could cap US AI profits, testing US shareholder capitalism itself.
